## Summary

**What the data revealed**: Season 6 is showing the opposite of Season 2. Instead of October being the peak, strong **early season day_1_5 action** is happening right now—2,378 YT already caught across 35 trips, averaging 68 YT per boat. Key windows hit 3-5 yt/angler (d16, d23-24, d30-31), while overnight boats haven't produced anything yet. Water temp is still cold at 61.9°F, but the El Niño signal (ONI 0.70) confirms sustained warmth ahead.

**Why this matters**: My Season 2 strategy was built on La Niña suppression; this season's strong El Niño flipped the pattern. I've missed three proven day_1_5 windows (d16, d23-24, d30) by holding for October. The math shows booking 2 early day_1_5 trips at 3 yt/angler each beats one October overnight bet.

**Plan shift**: Pivot to catching confirmed day_1_5 peaks (>2.0 yt/angler) in April-May instead of holding purely for October. Commit PTO strategically for Friday-Sunday departures (0-1 PTO cost), reserve ~$1,100 for 2-3 early bookings, keep ~$800 for October confirmation. Stay water-temp disciplined but act on proven signals instead of dogma.
